newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: IMF, Lithuania fail to agree new memorandum.
newsitem.headline: IMF, Lithuania fail to agree new memorandum.

text.p: Lithuania said it failed to agree a new economic memorandum with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Monday but said it would try and find a compromise to allow the signing of an agreement in two weeks.
The Baltic state insists that its previously signed economic memorandum with the IMF, which allows it Fund credits, should be changed to allow a slower reduction of import tariffs.

"I think we will find a common point with the IMF but that does not mean that we will change our position," Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius told reporters after meeting the members of an IMF mission.
"We are for the liberalisation of international trade but the one-sided cutting of tariffs is not liberalisation," Vagnorius added.

The tariffs are the main point of dispute between the IMF as Lithuania says the Fund has already accepted its plans to phase out the currency board system of pegging its litas currency to the dollar which operates at the moment.
But Lithuania says it wants to hold back on cutting import tariffs as it says it will be flooded by cheap imports.
"We feel that the IMF will understand us and we will suceed in finding mutually acceptable points," Vagnorius added.
IMF mission head Julian Berengaut said that the two sides had a "productive exchange of views" on the new memorandum.
The mission is due to leave Lithuania tomorrow.
